# Packistry

> Packistry is an open-source Composer registry for private PHP packages, licensed under GPL-3.0. It runs as a single
> Docker image (ghcr.io/packistry/packistry) that you can self-host, stores its data in SQLite, MySQL or PostgreSQL,
> and keeps package archives on disk or in S3.

Packistry imports packages from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Bitbucket and keeps them up to date through webhooks.
Packages can also be uploaded as zip files with a token that has write access. Composer installs packages from
Packistry like from any other Composer repository.

Packistry can mirror other Composer repositories, called upstreams, such as Packagist, a GitLab group registry,
Private Packagist, Satis or another Packistry. It caches the metadata and dists of mirrored packages, so
`composer install` keeps working while an upstream is down, and builds only need to reach Packistry.

Access is controlled with tokens. Deploy tokens for CI are scoped to repositories or single packages, and personal
tokens act on behalf of a user. Both have read or write access and an optional expiry date. Users can sign in with SSO through OpenID Connect
(for example Okta, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID), GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Google. Packistry records download
counts per package and shows 90-day download charts.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://packistryphp.com/docs/intro): what Packistry is and its main features
- [Installation](https://packistryphp.com/docs/installation): run Packistry with Docker, create a user, add sources and packages, and configure Composer and tokens
- [Concepts](https://packistryphp.com/docs/concepts): repositories, sources, packages, uploads, upstreams, deploy and personal tokens, users and roles, and authentication sources

## Guides

- [Upstream Mirroring](https://packistryphp.com/docs/guides/upstream-mirroring): mirror Packagist and private Composer repositories, credentials, filters and configuration
- [Behind a Reverse Proxy](https://packistryphp.com/docs/guides/behind-a-reverse-proxy): run Packistry behind a proxy that terminates TLS
- [Using MySQL Database](https://packistryphp.com/docs/guides/mysql): Docker Compose setup with MySQL
- [Store Package Archives in S3](https://packistryphp.com/docs/guides/store-archives-s3): keep package archives in S3-compatible storage
- [Deploy Packistry with Kamal](https://packistryphp.com/docs/guides/kamal): deploy with Kamal and a free TLS certificate

## Optional

- [CLI commands](https://packistryphp.com/docs/category/cli-commands): commands for users, repositories, sources, packages, tokens, mirror maintenance and cleanup
- [Source code](https://github.com/packistry/packistry): the Packistry repository on GitHub
